entityDescription: The Geodetic Cloud Computing Service (GCCS) was created in 2015 as a start-up company in the ESA Business Incubation Centre of Darmstadt (Germany). It forms primarily the operational platform that facilitates the distributed analysis of geodetic GNSS data by means of the GPSdancer software and solution approach. This analysis places any regional or global GNSS reference station in true global network solution time series, functionaly identical to the analysis of the International GNSS Service, but implemented in the form of a distributed computing system in the cloud. The key advantage of this approach is that there is no limit to the number of participating stations, while the data and products of individual stations remain private to the station operator. The GPSdancer solution approach has been developed over the period 2009-2015 in the form of a voluntary software development by a Working Group of the Reference Frame Commission of the International Association of Geodesy (IAG).

Niki Rotor Aviation delivers ready to fly gyroplanes that suite your particular flying preferences. The main priority for our team is your safety, comfort and unique personal experience with our gyroplanes. We provide opportunities that make your flight one of a kind. We like our partners and treat them as family members. Strong business relations are based on a friendly attitude, know-how and professional expertise.

Niki Rotor Aviation was created in 2010 in the Pravets. The company is known as a manufacturer of the first two-seater gyrocopter in Bulgaria.
In 2000, the company designed its first helicopter prototype. The machine was made of composite materials. Unfortunately, the helicopter does not reach the market potential required due to certain technical characteristics. However, the challenge of building a flying machine motivated the Rotor Team Aviation and in 2004 they started their new project – Gyrocopter for NIKI 2004.
Based on market research and observation, visiting many aviation shows world wide, Niki Rotor Aviation made all efforts required to make all dreams come true by manufacturing the first two-seated gyrocopter in Bulgaria.The body of the 2004 NIKI prototype was made of composite materials combined with plywood and aluminum. Gyrocopter NIKI 2004 successfully obtained the first flight test in December 2008 in Montana, Gabrovnitsa Airfield.
The improvements of NIKI 2004 set the new challenge in front of the company – the new prototype NIKI 2004 M ie APIS. This machine will be with the same design, but the cab will be with about 40 cm more.
Niki Rotor Aviation is working hard for the last couple of years and now the company is launching two brand new machines – Lighning and Kallithea. They combine very innovative elements, designers and constructive decisions. Both machines have one and the same cockpit and the main difference comes from the design of the tail and helix axis. New challenges ahead!

entityDescription: Over the next 10 years, a staggering 10000 new satellites will be launched; 70% of these are “Nano-Satellites”: they weigh less than 10Kg, cost under 100k$, and are revolutionising, and democratizing, access to space; most follow the first open-access standard in the space sector: the CubeSat standard. CubeSats are quickly acquiring new, varied and crucial functionalities: from high-speed communication networks, satellite internet, IoT, and earth observation, to space exploration. However, one last challenge remains a limiting factor: the lack of on-board propulsion. ienai SPACE, a newly-established company located in Madrid (Spain), aims to be a one-stop-shop for highly efficient ionic-liquid electric propulsion systems and mission analysis for nano-satellites. We will provide propulsion modules following the plug&play philosophy of CubeSats, but deeply customized for each particular platform and mission: from 2U to 12U; from RAAN-spacing to Earth-Moon transits or de-orbiting (aimed at containing the issue of space debris). Our versatile ATHENA Thruster is designed to be highly scalable in specific impulse and thrust; the technology is based on a novel iteration of electrospray thrusters, which boast some of the highest theoretical efficiencies for electric propulsion technologies in the low power range. In combination with its reduced form factor, this means less propellant on-board, making this technology attractive in constrained volumes. ienai SPACE uses a proprietary software for design and optimization of low-thrust trajectories which allows for concurrent engineering of both thruster and propulsive maneuvers. A software tool, ienai GO (go.ienai.space) has been developed to allow clients to perform preliminary analysis of propulsive requirements and maneuvers, in order to obtain a preliminary design of the optimal thruster. We also provide support to control activities during the mission, allowing these satellites to reach further, for longer.
